comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, loans increased by $19.8 billion due to higher loans in CIB and securities-based lending in AWM, while lending-related commitments decreased by $5.3 billion due to decreases in AWM and CCB, largely offset by higher commitments in CIB.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM report specific growth in their commercial/lending portfolios for 2024, attributing the increase to similar business lines. BAC reports a $28.1 billion (8%) increase in U.S. commercial loans, primarily driven by Global Markets and Global Banking. Similarly, JPM reports a $19.8 billion increase in loans, driven by higher loans in its Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB) and securities-based lending in its Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) division.

sentences.text: U.S. commercial loans increased $28.1 billion, or eight percent, during 2024 primarily driven by Global Markets and Global Banking.
As of December 31, 2024, loans increased $19.8 billion, driven by higher loans in CIB and higher securities-based lending in AWM.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the provision for credit losses on loans and lending commitments was $202 million, primarily driven by growth in the corporate loan portfolio and provisions for specific commercial real estate loans, partially offset by improvements in the macroeconomic outlook.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose drivers behind loan portfolio dynamics in 2024, though focusing on different financial metrics (growth vs. provisioning). BAC notes its U.S. commercial loan portfolio grew by $28.1 billion, driven by Global Markets and Global Banking. MS reports a $202 million provision for credit losses on loans and lending commitments, which was primarily related to growth in the corporate loan portfolio. Both companies highlight the expansion of their corporate/commercial lending activities as a key 2024 development.
